messages:
alyssa: heads up — product asked for a single consumer-facing metric we can show in the console: "token cost per 1k requests" + a clear line for cache savings attributed to each model. want to sync on feasibility and telemetry changes.

sam: sounds reasonable. main backend work is: emit per-invocation econ fields (model_sku, token_count, token_cost_usd, cache_hit_tokens). we already emit token_count for host infra but not cost or cache attribution per model.

mike: curious about sampling here — if we surface cost directly to customers we need low bias. full export for every invocation is expensive. can we do deterministic sampling keyed by tenant+day? :thinking_face:

jia: also UX note — if we show "cache savings" per model, it needs to line up with billing windows and routing fallbacks. customers will try to reconcile with bills. we should add an explanation tooltip + a hover breakdown: "raw tokens" vs "cached tokens" vs "amortized prefetch credits".

sam: agreed on sampling. proposal: 1% deterministic sample + aggregated counters for every tenant updated at 5m windows. counters have exact counts (no sampling) for cache_hit_tokens and total_tokens but we also stream sampled per-invocation rows to compute per-model unit economics for small tenants.

alyssa: that sounds complicated. can we sketch what would appear in console? mock: "Estimated cost per 1k requests: $X. Cache savings: $Y (Z% of tokens). Model mix: gpt-x: 60%, gpt-lite: 40%."

jia: +1 mock. UX question: when a model is used as fallback (e.g., quantized chain), who gets the credit for saved tokens? route owner or model owner? we need a deterministic allocation rule.

mike: we should allocate savings to the route that originated the invocation. if fallback triggers later in chain (tooling calls) then credit earlier route unless it's a different tenant. avoids double counting.

sam: technical detail: add fields to telemetry envelope: "origin_route", "model_sku", "invocation_role" (primary|fallback|tool) and "cache_hit_tokens". also emit a small provenance id for prefix-cache lookups so we can attribute prefetch vs hotpath.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: telemetry-v2 -> staging at 2024-01-11T15:02Z (sha: a1b2c3d).

alyssa: thanks — can we also add a "confidence" flag on the UI (low/medium/high) depending on sample coverage? customers asked for it.

sam: doable. confidence = sampled_rows / estimated_total_rows (bucketed). we'll expose that as string.

mike: throttles: make sure we don't let dashboards trigger rate-limited queries (big tenants). prefer precomputed aggregates in clickhouse and a per-tenant cached response.

jia: rollout plan suggestion: feature gated behind "econ_console_beta". start with internal-only for two weeks, then opt-in for SRE + three beta customers, then general availability. include reconciliation tests against billing data.

alyssa: owners: sam for telemetry schema + ingestion changes, mike for aggregation and sampling infra, jia for console UX + rollout. timeline: internal beta in 3 weeks?

sam: can do ingestion+schema in 2w, but will need a short follow-up to finalize sampling rates.

mike: I'll create an infra ticket for the 5m aggregation pipeline and tenant cache.

jia: I'll prototype the mock panels and tooltip copy this week.

alyssa: cool. next sync Fri EOD. action items: sam -> PR schema, mike -> infra ticket, jia -> UI mock. tagging @sam @mike @jia. :thumbsup:

sam: noted. linking a small example of emitted envelope (for review):

```
{ origin_route: "/chat/generate", tenant_id: "T123", model_sku: "gpt-x-16k", token_count: 420, token_cost_usd: 0.0036, cache_hit_tokens: 120, invocation_role: "primary" }
```

mike: one more: add utc_day field for deterministic sampling and aggregation keys.

alyssa: perfect. I'll drop the mock and the rollout plan into the RFC doc and move this to triage. thanks all. :raised_hands:
